part.goodBadBishop.title: Good and bad bishop
part.goodBadBishop.summary: See which bishop its own pawns shut in, and bring it outside the chain or trade it; the position decides when a bad bishop is still worth a lot.
ex.gb.jsLeZ: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.gb.jsLeZ.hint: Your central pawns stand on dark squares: see how far the bishop gets on the light ones.
ex.gb.jsLeZ.solution: 33.Bf7#! The good bishop goes to f7 and gives mate: the queen on f6 controls g7 and h8 and defends the bishop. The white pawns on c3, d4 and e5 stand on dark squares, and the light squares are free for the bishop.
ex.gb.YZ1WF: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.gb.YZ1WF.hint: See which dark squares around the black king the bishop on e6 can defend.
ex.gb.YZ1WF.solution: 26.dxe5#! The pawn captures the knight on e5 with check and mate. The black bishop on e6, stuck on the light squares behind its pawns, defends none of the dark squares around the king.
ex.gb.x1Cgu: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.gb.x1Cgu.hint: Your pawns on e5 and f4 stand on dark squares: look at the open diagonals of the bishop that has not moved yet.
ex.gb.x1Cgu.solution: 18.Bb5#! The bishop on f1, which had not yet moved, enters b5 along the open diagonal and gives mate: the queen on c5 and the knight on c7 control the king's other squares. The bad bishop on c8, shut in behind its pawns, cannot block the check.
ex.gb.luh36: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.gb.luh36.hint: Your pawns all stand on dark squares: look for a light square for the bishop near the black king.
ex.gb.luh36.solution: 38.Bg6#! The bishop goes to g6 and gives mate, defended by the rook on d6; the rook and the queen control the king's other squares. The white pawns all stand on dark squares, and the good bishop moves freely on the light ones.
ex.gb.tH8CQ: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.gb.tH8CQ.hint: See what the queen on b6 attacks if the bishop on d6 gets out of the way.
ex.gb.tH8CQ.solution: 22...Bxh2+! The good bishop captures the pawn on h2 with check along the open dark diagonal, and the queen on b6 now attacks the queen on e6. After 23.Kxh2 Qxe6, Black wins the queen.
ex.gb.VXVLB: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.gb.VXVLB.hint: The black queen on g3 has few squares, and the rook on h3 depends on it.
ex.gb.VXVLB.solution: 20.Be1! The bishop on d2 looks bad, shut in behind the pawns on e3 and b4, but on e1 it gains an open diagonal to g3 and attacks the queen, the defender of the rook on h3. After 20...Qc7 21.gxh3, White wins the rook.
ex.gb.1b4gU: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.gb.1b4gU.hint: The white queen on h5 has few free squares.
ex.gb.1b4gU.solution: 23...Bg4! The bishop attacks the queen on h5, which has no square to escape to. After 24.Qxg4 Qxg4, Black wins the queen for the bishop. By the colour of the pawns the bishop on f5 would be bad, but outside the chain it leaves the queen without a square.
ex.gb.vw53v: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.gb.vw53v.hint: See what stands on the diagonal from the queen on a4 to e8.
ex.gb.vw53v.solution: 13.Bb5! The good bishop leaves e2 along the open diagonal and pins the queen on d7 to the king on e8, backed by the queen on a4. After 13...Qxb5 14.Nxb5 axb5 15.Qxa8+, White wins the queen and the rook for the bishop and the knight.
ex.gb.dia3S: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.gb.dia3S.hint: Look for the dark diagonal that links the white queen to the king.
ex.gb.dia3S.solution: 19...Bb6! The black pawns on c6 and d5 stand on light squares, and the good bishop on c7 has the dark ones free: it pins the queen on d4 to the king on g1. After 20.Kh1 Bxd4, Black wins the queen for the bishop.
part.bishopPair.title: Bishop against knight and the bishop pair
part.bishopPair.summary: In an open position, the bishops and the bishop pair are worth more; in a closed position, with an outpost, the knight can be better. The position decides.
ex.bp.BJugQ: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.bp.BJugQ.hint: Your two bishops have open diagonals to the black king.
ex.bp.BJugQ.solution: 19.Bh6#! The bishop goes to h6 and gives mate: it controls g7, and the bishop on d5 controls f7 and g8. With the bishop pair, White covers the squares of both colours around the king.
ex.bp.Ovt4y: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.bp.Ovt4y.hint: Your two bishops are close to the black king: see which squares each one controls.
ex.bp.Ovt4y.solution: 31.Bxf6#! The bishop on e7 captures the pawn on f6 with check and mate: it controls g7, and the bishop on e6 controls g8. Together, the two bishops cover the squares of both colours around the king.
ex.bp.VMK6x: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.bp.VMK6x.hint: The knight on g3 stands on an outpost, defended by the pawn on f4, and the white pawns shut in the bishop on e2.
ex.bp.VMK6x.solution: 34...Nh1#! The knight on g3 jumps to h1 and gives mate: the rook on b1 controls the first rank, and the pawns on d4 and f4 take e3 and g3 from the king. The bad bishop on e2, shut in behind the pawns on f3 and g2, does not reach h1.
ex.bp.wxf2f: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.bp.wxf2f.hint: The knight on b5 stands on an outpost, and the black bishop on d8 moves on the dark squares, like the pawns on c5, d6 and e5.
ex.bp.wxf2f.solution: 40.Na7#! The knight on b5 jumps to a7 and gives mate: the rook on h7 controls b7, c7 and d7, and the rook on b8 blocks the king's exit. The bad bishop on d8 does not control a7.
ex.bp.Tueez: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.bp.Tueez.hint: The bishop on e3 already controls the dark squares next to the white king. The other bishop still needs a way in.
ex.bp.Tueez.solution: 19...Qxh3+! The queen captures the bishop on h3, and after 20.Rxh3 Bxh3#, the bishop on c8 gives mate: it controls g2, and the bishop on e3 controls f2 and g1. The bishop pair covers the squares of both colours around the king.
ex.bp.7GQjt: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.bp.7GQjt.hint: The bishop on d3 already controls h7. Open the diagonal of the other bishop to the king.
ex.bp.7GQjt.solution: 32.Qxh6+! The queen captures the pawn on h6, and after 32...gxh6 33.Bxf6#, the bishop on c3 gives mate along the diagonal to h8, and the bishop on d3 controls h7. Together, the two bishops leave the king no square.
ex.bp.z3FEP: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.bp.z3FEP.hint: Look for a square from which the bishop attacks two black pieces at the same time.
ex.bp.z3FEP.solution: 32.Be7! The bishop makes a double attack on the rook on d8 and the knight on f6. After 32...Re8 33.Bxf6, White wins the knight. In the open position, the long-range bishop attacks both pieces at once.
ex.bp.Y34di: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.bp.Y34di.hint: Your two bishops aim at the white king along diagonals of both colours.
ex.bp.Y34di.solution: 21...Bg3+! The dark-squared bishop gives check, and the king only has h1. After 22.Kh1, 22...Bxg2#: the bishop on b7 captures the pinned bishop on g2, and the queen on f2 defends the bishop and controls g1.
ex.bp.a43Yq: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.bp.a43Yq.hint: Your two bishops can take away every square from the rook on c8.
ex.bp.a43Yq.solution: 21.Bb7! The bishop attacks the rook on c8, and it has no square: the bishop on g3 controls b8 and c7, and the one on b7 controls a8 and c6. After 21...Rc7 22.Bxc7, White wins the rook for the bishop.
